title: CareerLoop Core Mock — Set 01
patternNote: CareerLoop core mock covering Mathematics, General Intelligence & Reasoning, General Science, English Language and General Awareness. 30 original questions written for CareerLoop / 30 minutes / +1 per correct / −0.33 per wrong.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3². The LCM takes the highest power of each prime: 2² × 3² = 36.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an item at ₹800 and gives a 25% discount. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Discount = 25% of 800 = ₹200. Selling price = 800 − 200 = ₹600.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7 and their difference is 12. What is the smaller number?
questions.explanation: The difference of the ratio parts is 2, so one part is 12 ÷ 2 = 6. The smaller number is 5 × 6 = 30.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: What is the average of the first ten natural numbers?
questions.explanation: The sum of 1 to 10 is 55, and 55 ÷ 10 = 5.5. Equivalently, the average of the first n natural numbers is (n + 1)/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: If two-fifths of a number is 48, what is the number?
questions.explanation: If 2/5 of the number is 48, then 1/5 is 24 and the whole number is 24 × 5 = 120.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: One pipe can fill a tank in 6 hours and another in 12 hours. Working together, how long will they take?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 tank per hour. Time = 4 hours.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: An article bought for ₹500 is sold for ₹600. What is the profit percentage?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is 60 m and its length is 18 m. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2(l + b), so 60 = 2(18 + b) and b = 12 m. Area = 18 × 12 = 216 m².

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Find the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10 — consecutive even numbers. The next difference is 12, so 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Find the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, 27 = 3³ and 64 = 4³ are perfect cubes. 100 is a perfect square, not a cube.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: If CAT = 24 by adding letter positions (C = 3, A = 1, T = 20), what is DOG?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: A person facing north turns 90° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: From north, a clockwise (right) turn of 90° points east.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: A is B's sister and C is B's mother. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: If C is B's mother, then C is also the mother of A, who is B's sister. So A is C's daughter.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Hand : Fingers :: Foot : ?
questions.explanation: Fingers are the digits of the hand; toes are the digits of the foot.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Complete the series: 1, 4, 9, 16, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are the squares of 1, 2, 3, 4. The next term is 5² = 25.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.stem: Which letter is fifth to the right of the tenth letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The tenth letter from the left is J. Moving five places right gives O (10 + 5 = 15th letter).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.stem: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). Joule is energy, watt is power and pascal is pressure.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.stem: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explanation: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, written H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.stem: Which cell organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP through respiration, hence 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.stem: Which gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.stem: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 3 × 10⁸ metres per second in vacuum, roughly 300,000 km/s.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.stem: Deficiency of vitamin C causes which disease?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy. Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency and night blindness by vitamin A deficiency.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'brave'.
questions.explanation: 'Brave' means showing courage, so 'courageous' is the synonym. The other options mean the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'victory'.
questions.explanation: 'Victory' means a win; its opposite is 'defeat'. 'Success', 'win' and 'triumph' are synonyms.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Fill in the blank: He is good ______ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after 'good' when describing a skill is 'at': good at mathematics.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'necessary' — one c, double s, and 'ary' at the end.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: What does the idiom 'a piece of cake' mean?
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' means something very easy to do.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What is the national bird of India?
questions.explanation: The Indian peacock was declared the national bird of India in 1963.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: Japan uses the yen. Won is Korea, yuan is China and ringgit is Malaysia.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who is known as the 'Missile Man of India'?
questions.explanation: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam is known as the Missile Man of India for his work on India's missile programmes.
